narrative.text: Four Kravenstal collieries went silent on the same morning. It wasn't a wildcat strike—it was a coordinated shutdown. The workers aren't demanding higher wages; they are demanding the nationalization of the mines. Stefan Morvec arrives at the Palace unannounced, brushing past your security detail with the ease of a man who owns the building.

Chancellor. You have a problem in Kravenstal. I can end it by Thursday. My foremen have the authority to send the men back down the shaft. All I ask is that you reconsider the new mining safety regulations your Labor Ministry is drafting. They are... economically unviable.

Morvec orchestrated the strike to leverage me. He wants me to drop the safety regulations in exchange for him ordering his foremen to break the strike. If I accept, I prove the workers' chants are true: the state answers to Morvec. If I refuse, the Kravenstal economy stalls, and I lose the workers' support anyway.

If we let Morvec handle this, we surrender the province to him. If we send in the police, we become Halvek. We have one other option: send Gregor Marić to negotiate directly with the workers' council, bypassing Morvec entirely. It's slower, and it might fail, but it keeps the state sovereign.

choices.text: Accept Morvec's offer. Drop the safety regulations. End the strike now.
Refuse Morvec. Send Marić to negotiate with the workers directly. The state doesn't ask oligarchs for permission to govern.
Threaten to nationalize the mines if the strike isn't resolved by Friday. Call Morvec's bluff.

narrative.text: A wise decision, Chancellor. The men will be back at work by morning. We will discuss the regulations later.
Morvec leaves. The strike will end, but the cost is written in the safety regulations you just sacrificed.
I bought peace with the lives of the miners. Morvec knows it. The workers know it. And now, I have to live with it.

choices.text: The economy is stable. That is all that matters today.

narrative.text: You are making a mistake, Ashavel. The workers do not listen to ministers. They listen to their foremen. And their foremen listen to me.
Morvec leaves in a fury. Marić boards a train to Kravenstal within the hour. The outcome is uncertain, but the state is fighting its own battle.

choices.text: We will see who the workers listen to.

narrative.text: Nationalize? You would bankrupt the state trying to run my mines. If you try it, I will close every factory in Veltria by the weekend.
It is an open threat of a capital strike. Morvec leaves, and the battle lines are drawn. The workers cheer the threat of nationalization, but the markets panic.

choices.text: Let him close them. The Republic will survive without Morvec.
